evidence.claim: Zwingenberger's official chronology gives his birth as May 7, 1955 in Hamburg and lists his first Boogie Woogie Breakdown and Boogie Woogie Session '76 recordings in May 1976.
The chronology records a May 1978 Los Angeles session with Big Joe Turner at Johnny Otis's studio and an April-May 1980 European tour with Lionel Hampton.

axel-zwingenberger.limitations: The artist chronology provides months and titles, not full personnel matrices or individual track dates.
axel-zwingenberger.summary: Hamburg-born boogie-woogie pianist Axel Zwingenberger began recording in 1976 and recorded with Big Joe Turner in Los Angeles in May 1978.
axel-zwingenberger.why_it_matters: His dated artist chronology gives traceable early sessions and international collaborations.

evidence.claim: McAll's official biography says he studied at Victorian College of the Arts with Paul Grabowsky and Mike Nock, moved to New York during the 1990s, and co-founded Groove Collective.
His leader discography lists Mooroolbark (ABC Jazz, 2015) and Hearing The Blood (Extra Celestial Arts, 2017).

barney-mcall.limitations: The page's large discography includes later reissues and collaborations; no single recording-session personnel are inferred.
barney-mcall.summary: Australian pianist Barney McAll co-founded Groove Collective after moving to New York in the 1990s and released the leader albums Mooroolbark and Hearing the Blood.
barney-mcall.why_it_matters: Artist-authored career chronology directly connects his New York ensemble work with independently dated recordings.

evidence.claim: Barth's official biography says that after arriving in New York in 1988 he began playing in the bands of Stanley Turrentine and Terence Blanchard.
His official biography reports that his trio recorded live at New York's Village Vanguard, and lists the 2022 Origin Records trio album Dedication with Montez Coleman and Vicente Archer.

bruce-barth.limitations: The artist biography does not specify the trio's Village Vanguard recording dates or personnel.
bruce-barth.summary: Jazz pianist Bruce Barth worked with Stanley Turrentine and Terence Blanchard after moving to New York in 1988; his trio recorded live at the Village Vanguard.
bruce-barth.why_it_matters: Barth's own biography names his formative band jobs and a documented live trio recording instead of generic jazz credentials.

evidence.claim: Forman's official biography identifies Cow Bop as his western-bebop band and names its albums Swingin' Out West, Route 66, Too Hick for the Room, and Cowlifornia Swing.
The same biography credits Forman with soundtrack performances in three Clint Eastwood films and specifically names Million Dollar Baby.

bruce-forman.limitations: The source does not establish specific soundtrack cues played by Forman.
bruce-forman.summary: Jazz guitarist Bruce Forman leads the western-bebop band Cow Bop and recorded soundtrack performances for three Clint Eastwood films, including Million Dollar Baby.
bruce-forman.why_it_matters: The musician's original account identifies a specific style-crossing ensemble and film-session career.

evidence.claim: Dulfer's official biography states that she founded her own band at age 13 and that her first solo album Saxuality received a Grammy nomination.
Her official discography dates Saxuality to 1990, Sax-A-Go-Go to 1993 and Big Girl to 1995.

candy-dulfer.limitations: The Grammy reference is a nomination, not a win; no exact award category is asserted.
candy-dulfer.summary: Dutch saxophonist Candy Dulfer began leading a band at 13; her 1990 solo debut Saxuality received a Grammy nomination.
candy-dulfer.why_it_matters: Official biography and catalog identify the early leadership and pivotal debut without guessing specific track performers.

evidence.claim: Wackerman's official biography says he joined the Bill Watrous Refuge West Big Band in 1978 and spent seven years working with Frank Zappa.
His biography credits eight recorded albums with Allan Holdsworth and identifies his leader album Forty Reasons as featuring Holdsworth, Jimmy Johnson and Jim Cox.

chad-wackerman.limitations: The site's total album counts are the artist's own claims and do not resolve alternate release editions.
chad-wackerman.summary: Drummer Chad Wackerman toured and recorded with Frank Zappa for seven years and worked extensively with guitarist Allan Holdsworth, including eight albums.
chad-wackerman.why_it_matters: Official first-person discography establishes two sustained fusion/rock collaborations and named solo albums.

evidence.claim: Fulton's official album credits state Meet Me at Birdland was recorded September 2-4, 2022 at Birdland Theater in New York, with Fulton on piano and vocals, Hide Tanaka on bass and Fukushi Tainaka on drums.
The pianist's official discography describes Sometimes I'm Happy as recorded April 10-11, 2008 at Avatar Studio in New York, with Neal Miner on bass and Fukushi Tainaka on drums.

champian-fulton.limitations: The album promotion also cites awards; none are needed to substantiate the recording credit.
champian-fulton.summary: Jazz pianist and singer Champian Fulton recorded Meet Me at Birdland live in September 2022 with Hide Tanaka and Fukushi Tainaka.
champian-fulton.why_it_matters: First-party album credits document the dates, room, and rhythm-section personnel of a specific live recording.

evidence.claim: Stryker's official biography identifies him as a sideman with Stanley Turrentine and Jack McDuff.
His Strikezone Records discography lists Groove Street (2024) featuring Bob Mintzer and Stryker's working trio with organist Jared Gold and drummer McClenty Hunter.

dave-stryker.limitations: Homepage promotional claims about radio-chart success are omitted; album/year and named ensemble are explicit.
dave-stryker.summary: Jazz guitarist Dave Stryker played with Stanley Turrentine and Jack McDuff; his 2024 Groove Street paired his organ trio with saxophonist Bob Mintzer.
dave-stryker.why_it_matters: Stryker's own label catalog links long sideman experience to a specifically identified 2024 quartet recording.

evidence.claim: Abate's official biography states he played lead alto saxophone in Ray Charles's orchestra for two years during the mid-1970s and tenor saxophone in the revived Artie Shaw Orchestra in 1986-87.
The biography identifies Live at Birdland NYC (1991, Candid Jazz) as his first CD and names James Williams, Rufus Reid and Kenny Washington as its trio.

greg-abate.limitations: The account provides year spans, not exact session dates; no precise recording date is claimed.
greg-abate.summary: Saxophonist Greg Abate played lead alto in Ray Charles's orchestra and tenor sax in the revived Artie Shaw Orchestra before recording as a leader.
greg-abate.why_it_matters: Official artist biography names his instrumental roles, bandleader tenures and first leader-session personnel.

evidence.claim: Cole's official biography describes Temptation as an album consisting exclusively of material written by Tom Waits.
Cole's official biography identifies Aaron Davis on piano, George Koller bass, Davide Direnzo drums and John Johnson saxophone among the ensemble recording Dark Moon.

holly-cole.limitations: The current official biography supports Dark Moon ensemble membership; it does not confirm a 2019 Montreal original-trio session.
holly-cole.summary: Canadian jazz vocalist Holly Cole recorded the Tom Waits songbook Temptation and teamed with pianist Aaron Davis on Dark Moon.
holly-cole.why_it_matters: The singer's own published biography distinguishes her Tom Waits repertoire concept from specific pianist and ensemble performance credits on Dark Moon.

evidence.claim: Terrasson's official biography says he was born in Berlin in 1965, grew up in Paris and went to Berklee College of Music.
His official biography states he won the 1993 Thelonious Monk competition, then toured with Betty Carter and signed to Blue Note the following year.

jacky-terrasson.limitations: The biography gives a competition year but no exact contest date; it is not used to assign specific recording sessions.
jacky-terrasson.summary: Paris-raised jazz pianist Jacky Terrasson won the 1993 Thelonious Monk piano competition, toured with Betty Carter and subsequently signed to Blue Note.
jacky-terrasson.why_it_matters: His published bilingual biography supplies a precise career turning point and label transition.
